issues.description: Attribute 'Book.author' has a type mismatch: the problem statement specifies Book.author should be a String (problem statement: 'A struct Book consists of two Strings title and author'), but the solution implementation declares Book.author as a Bool. The template file only contains task placeholders and does not implement the struct. This inconsistency will cause compilation errors and confusion because the solution code (Client.assembleBookstore) constructs Book instances using String authors (e.g. "Stephen King"), while the Book struct in the solution expects a Bool. Students following the problem specification or the template will implement author as String, but the provided solution code's Book definition will not match, preventing tests or example code from compiling and making the expected type unclear.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the type of the 'author' property in the Book struct in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift from Bool to String so it matches the problem specification. Update the declaration to: 'let author: String'. Ensure any Book initializations in the solution (Client.assembleBookstore) remain String literals for the author (no further changes required there). This will restore consistency between the problem statement, template intent, and solution implementation and prevent compilation errors.
